question.question:
A trader shorts 100000 units of base currency quoted at USD 1.235 per unit, closing 26 days later at USD 1.26. Notional = units x open rate, fixed throughout. Annual rates: base 0%, USD 5.75%. The short pays the base rate and receives the USD rate: daily gross carry = notional x (USD rate - base rate)/360, positive when earned. Every day the broker also deducts a financing markup of 0.5% per year on notional, whatever the sign. Daily net carry = gross minus markup; if positive it is capped at USD 60 per day, negatives are not floored. Total carry = daily net carry x days. Price P&L = (open - close) x units. Add carry and price P&L, deduct a USD 10 commission, then charge a 20% performance fee only if the post-commission amount is positive. Report the net total P&L in USD, negative for a loss.

Answer format: return only the exact numeric value interpreted in `usd`, using finite-decimal notation when it terminates in base 10 and an irreducible `numerator/denominator` fraction otherwise, with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: Signed daily net carry after markup and cap, USD per day
Signed total carry over the holding period in USD
Signed price P&L of the short position in USD
